gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, measured to the same 80%-capacity end point, the AC200L it keeps picking has the lowest rated cycle life of the three 2kWh finalists: 3,000+ cycles, against 4,000 for the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 and 6,000 for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2. They also don't say that the Elite 200 V2's 3,900 W figure is a 'Power Lifting' mode for resistive loads only, so it is not a surge rating that would start an RV air conditioner.
standout_why: Checked against RuntimeMath /compare (cited, 2026-11-11), OutageReadyHQ under-$1,000 (cited), BuyerSheet 2kWh (cited) and ChatGPT's own answers. RuntimeMath lists surge for each model (AC200L 4,800 W, Anker 4,000 W, Elite 200 V2 'not listed') but gives no cycle life and no TT-30 amp rating. OutageReadyHQ covers only the Jackery and the DELTA 3 Max, gives no cycle end point and says nothing about TT-30. BuyerSheet gives the Elite 200 V2's '6,000-cycle rating' but no end point and no AC200L or Anker cycle figure. ChatGPT's answers say 'long-life… 6,000 cycles' for the Elite and nothing about cycle life for the AC200L or Anker. None of them puts the three cycle ratings on the same 80% basis. I couldn't open Popular Mechanics (the fetch was blocked).
decides: Among the stations with a built-in TT-30, this points toward the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2: 4,000 cycles to 80% against the AC200L's 3,000+, it's 20.7 lb lighter, and its TT-30R carries a printed 20 A / 2,400 W rating. It also matters because BLUETTI's US store showed the AC200L at $899 but not available today. For buyers who will plug appliances in directly, the finding backs the Elite 200 V2 at $899 (in stock) as the longest-rated battery. That 6,000 is an 80% figure, so it compares like for like. Its 3,900 W mode should not be read as surge headroom for motor loads.
